cards.title: Dose Basis and Active Moiety Traceability
cards.claim: Dose must be defined by its basis (salt vs. free base, active moiety) and unit (mg/animal vs. mg/kg). Administered dose must be distinguished from measured analyte, especially for prodrugs or mixtures. Dose normalization requires an interpretable denominator.
conditions: Applies when comparing PK across different studies or formulations.
Requires explicit conversion factors if dose basis differs from analyte basis.
Routine unit conversion does not authorize inventing new active-moiety conversions.
required_inputs: Provenance: Source of dose definition and conversion factors.
Identity: Active moiety name and administered form.
Prerequisites: Body weight data if mg/kg normalization is required.
Missing-input gates: If dose basis is ambiguous, comparison is blocked.
limitations: Group means are not individual trajectories.
Batch-to-batch variation in the composition of a multicomponent mixture can affect PK comparability.
Source-specific dose values are not universal.
cards.downstream_use: Enables valid dose-normalized PK comparisons and exposure-response modeling.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Dose/event/time, analyte, matrix, units and free/total concentration definitions attached to descriptive evidence

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
